title: Telemetry-guided embedding onboarding and tenant-aware gradual rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Safely onboard new embedding models behind the reranking gateway with telemetry-driven quality and latency gates, per-tenant gradual exposure, and automated rollback triggers. We need a repeatable flow for adding candidate models to the catalog, running A/B evaluations, and promoting/retiring variants while preserving SLOs for latency and semantic fidelity. This ticket implements the gating, metrics instrumentation, and a tenant-aware traffic gradualizer for initial soft launches.
background: Recent embedding rollouts revealed two failure modes: (1) semantic regressions for a subset of tenants caused poor rerank quality, and (2) bursts in tokenization/encoding CPU on shared nodes increased tail latency. Current onboarding is manual: PRs + ad-hoc canary tenants. We need automated telemetry to detect quality regressions (embedding similarity drift, downstream rerank delta) and a mechanism to throttle per-tenant traffic during rollout so noisy tenants do not amplify regressions.
solution_overview: - Add per-request telemetry hooks in the reranking gateway: record embed model id, encode latency, tokenization time, and kv-cache hit/miss. - Implement a candidate evaluator service that computes semantic drift metrics vs baseline (cosine delta distribution, recall@k changes on holdout queries), and rolling P50/P95 latency deltas. - Build a tenant-aware gradualizer that assigns a rollout weight per tenant and supports step-up/step-down with backoff based on quality and latency signals. - Wire automatic safety fences: if quality drops beyond threshold or latency SLO breached for >5m, reduce weight to last stable step and create alert/auto-rollback proposal.
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow traffic for candidate model across 1000 synthetic holdout queries + 1% real traffic to collect initial metrics. 2) Run 24h automatic prober evaluating semantic metrics and latencies. 3) Soft-open: enable candidate at 5% weight for low-risk tenants (by usage and SLA) for 2h. 4) Gradually step to 25% then 50% with 15m observation windows and gating. 5) Full promotion after 72h stable signals. 6) Schedule deprecation window for old model with tenant pinning option.
metrics_and_alerts: - Semantic metrics: cosine_delta_median, cosine_delta_95, recall_at_10_delta, rerank_agreement_fraction. - Latency metrics: embed_encode_p50, embed_encode_p95, rerank_infer_p95. - Resource metrics: encode_cpu_pct_by_node, kv_cache_hit_rate. - Alerts: quality_fence_breach (cosine_delta_95 > 0.12 or recall_at_10_delta < -0.05 sustained 15m), latency_slo_violation (embed_encode_p95 > 150ms for >5m), tenant_amplifier_detected (one tenant contributes >30% of candidate errors).
acceptance_criteria: Candidate telemetry emitted on 100% of rerank requests in shadow and canary modes
Candidate evaluator computes and stores semantic and latency deltas within 5 minutes of traffic ingestion
Tenant gradualizer can target tenants by label and adjust weights automatically based on policy
Automated rollback triggers when quality_fence_breach or latency_slo_violation fire; rollbacks verified in staging
Runbook documented and linked; PM and Design sign-off obtained
tasks: Instrument rerank gateway: add embed_model_id, encode_time_ms, tokenization_time_ms, kv_cache_hit boolean
Ship candidate evaluator microservice and metrics pipeline (kafka -> prober -> timeseries)
Implement tenant gradualizer with persistent state and API for step policies
Integrate rollback hooks with rollout controller and PagerDuty alerts
Create per-tenant cohort selection UI in Console for selects and overrides (coordinate with PM/Design)
Smoke test on staging with synthetic traffic and chaos pod to validate rollback path
Add e2e SLO tests to CI for a sample tenant matrix
risks_mitigations: Risk: False positives in semantic drift due to query distribution shift. Mitigation: maintain per-tenant baselines and require multiple signals (cosine + rerank_agreement) before gating.
Risk: Increased telemetry volume causing backend pressure. Mitigation: sample shadow payloads and use compact histograms; add adaptive sampling by tenant.
Risk: Tenants with heavy tail traffic amplify regressions. Mitigation: tenant-aware caps and emergency circuit breakers; quarterly review of hot tenants.
